technique_name: Describe the effects of the Indian Removal Act of 1830.
description: The Indian Removal Act of 1830 was a federal law that authorized the U.S. president to negotiate with Native American tribes for the exchange of their land east of the Mississippi River in exchange for territory to the west. This law led to the relocation of thousands of Native Americans, who were forcibly removed from their ancestral homelands and marched to their relocation destination, often enduring great hardship and brutality. Many Native Americans were either killed in the process or died
